# Content Summary
The provided content is a comprehensive documentation snippet for Universal Ctags, a maintained implementation of the `ctags` tool. Universal Ctags is designed to generate an index or tag file of language objects found in source files, facilitating easy navigation for text editors and other tools. This project continues the development of Exuberant Ctags, which introduced multi-language support and user-defined language parsing capabilities but became inactive over time.

Key features of Universal Ctags include enhanced language support, an extended optlib for defining new language parsers via command line, and an experimental interactive mode. The documentation provides detailed instructions for obtaining the latest builds across different platforms, including Windows, Unix-like systems, Mac, and Snap packages. It also outlines the build and installation process using Autotools, with references to additional documentation for platform-specific instructions.

The manual section emphasizes the importance of consulting the man pages for primary documentation, while the Universal Ctags Hacking Guide offers additional insights for developers. Differences from Exuberant Ctags are highlighted, such as changes in configuration file loading and stricter rules for kind letters and names, necessitating updates for users transitioning from Exuberant Ctags.
